transcript: This play takes place entirely in a single tent. The play is called camping and follows two friends over the course of decades of their life and their various meetings inside this tent, with their first meeting being in high school and their last being well into adulthood. Our two main characters are Brit, played by Alice Kremelberg, and Ari, played by Colby Minifie, who some of you may know from the boys. These characters are messy and flawed, and they both capture that complexity really well. Their performances and chemistry is a big reason why this play works as well as it does. A big part of this play is the will they, won't they sexual tension between these two characters. Growing up in a very small, conservative trailer park community where everything is kind of done one specific way and people don't really leave, this tent provides them with a space where they can escape from the outside world and a space where they could be open and honest with each other, but maybe not themselves. And we, the audience, are a fly on the wall for these very intimate conversations. I personally found this play to be very gripping from start to finish. It is only 85 minutes, but I found it flew by. And while it does drag its feet a bit towards the end, it did feel coming out of it that I had lived a life alongside these characters. And it is the kind Of play that can only work in the intimacy of a tiny off-Broadway theatre. And so, with all of that said, camping is going to be a Broadway Ben recommendation.
